candidate_relations.reason: The transbronchial biopsy demonstrated classic organizing pneumonia histology (granulation tissue filling alveoli, interstitial inflammation, intra-alveolar fibrin). While tacrolimus can rarely cause lung toxicity, the biopsy findings and clinical context (post-PCP infection, peribronchovascular consolidations) point to organizing pneumonia as the diagnosis, not a drug-induced pneumonitis. Asserting tacrolimus causation conflicts with the established histopathologic diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Tacrolimus-induced pneumonitis is a drug-toxicity etiology, not the histopathologic pattern of organizing pneumonia confirmed on biopsy

candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy confirmed organizing pneumonia histology, and the clinical sequence (new consolidations appearing after PCP treatment with resolution of the original infection) supports a post-infectious organizing pneumonia pattern. This is a complete equivalent of the reference diagnosis with an allowable etiologic specification.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Organizing pneumonia with post-infectious etiology is fully consistent with the reference; the etiologic qualifier is additive and compatible

case_quality_flags: Paradoxical worsening after PCP treatment with new consolidations and negative repeat BAL strongly supports post-infectious organizing pneumonia as the unifying diagnosis
